This game is phenomenal. I didn't get it when it first came out because of zombie game fatigue, but thank god the YouTube algorithm brought it back around this year because I absolutely lost myself in it. I could write a ton about how great this game is in so many areas, but I'm too stoned for that.

All I'm gonna say is this game greatly surpassed my expectations on many levels from the excellent pacing to the emotional weight of the story to the thrill of working your way up to horde slaying, all set against an several absolutely gorgeous, dynamic, Pacific Northwest landscape that you rip through on your post apocalyptic bike... its badass as fuck.

Deacon St. John, an Afghanistan war vet, enforcer for a motorcycle club turned lover turned drifting survivor made for a complex, morally conflicting, deeply flawed but ultimately lovable badass of a character. His progression and story arch is quite significant, and while he never loses his more troubling baggage, his humanity outshines what you have to do in the shit. I hear some of the complaints about his character, but I think now that the launch is days gone, sentiments about his character will have changed. Its been a blast slaying hordes and silencing marauders as St John, Deacon St John.

I hope this game gets enough love long term for a sequel. It deserves it for sure

If you're on the fence about purchasing Days Gone, let me make it simple for you: Buy this game, you will not regret it. This open-world action-adventure game is a thrilling ride from start to finish.

Now, let's talk about the hordes. Initially, the thought of facing hundreds of Freakers at once was terrifying. But as you progress through the game, you develop strategies and acquire weapons that make these encounters less daunting. **I'm not afraid of the hordes anymore :-)**, and that's a testament to how well the game evolves and empowers the player.

In conclusion, Days Gone is a fantastic game that offers a rich, immersive experience. The combination of a gripping story, a detailed world, and intense gameplay makes it a must-buy. Buy this game, you will not regret it, and soon, you'll be conquering those hordes with confidence just like I did.

Wow. I heard about the launch problems and how buggy this game was on launch. Picked it up in a recent steam sale and decided to try it out.

Totally exceeded all expectations. They weren't low - I had heard how much praise the game was getting since it was free in PS+ and also how amazing it was since the PC version released. Just never really seemed like a game to hold my attention... I was wrong.

Graphics are so good. So much care and love were out into every little detail visually.
The gameplay is fun, never feels tedious at all, even driving from point a to b is very fun, listening to all the dialogue and story bits as you go, which brings me to another thing...
The voice acting is so exceptional, so beyond what you would expect from a video game. The characters talk like people. They feel like people. I am usually more of a fan of games like Stalker, FPS games, competitive shooters, so for someone like me to actually CARE about the dialogue and not skip anything is a HUGE accomplishment.

Buy this game if you've ever been curious about it. It's crazy how good it is.

Days Gone was one of the memorable gaming experiences of 2024. Personally I have been a huge fan of the Far Cry series, however the Far Cry worlds are slowly turning into highly unrealistic fantasy wonderlands. With Days Gone one was constantly without medkits, low on bullets, nearly broken bike low on fuel fighting truely terrifying hordes and abusive, greedy (still) human cunts that have stopped caring for fellow man.

There are mild annoyances, such as cut scenes on extracting meat from animals and the usual piperun formatted limitations on exploring the world itself completely openly - however, with the story, the beatiful original soundtrack country songs, good voice acting of the characters filled with sorrow from the loss of their closest ones you bond with the world, the people in it and really wish to help and support the small communities trying their best to survive in the aftermath.

So - all in all, get the game on download, put the kids to sleep and take a beer next to your gaming setup as it's one hell of a ride. Highly recommended. <3

Great game. Kept me engaged for hours. Good story to follow, with a relative amount of diverse content for an open world game. The hordes, especially early on, really challenge you.

This game quickly became one of my all-time favorites. The gameplay is fun, the gunplay feels solid, and the survival aspect is satisfying. Enemy variety is also surprisingly good for a zombie game.

The graphics are impressive, and the area where the game takes place is both beautiful and diverse.

But the true highlight for me is the characters and the story. The characters are incredibly well-written, they feel real, each with their own emotions, goals, and perspectives. The story, while a bit predictable at times, still delivers plenty of strong moments and plot twists. It’s honestly a shame we never got a sequel, because I genuinely want to see more of these characters. Such a great cast… and Deacon? He’s simply hot!

Hordes were super fun to take on, I’d be lying if I said I didn’t panic the first time I ran into one during my playthrough.

There’s also a good variety of extra game modes if you don’t feel like doing the campaign. Some of them can be quite challenging if you’re aiming for gold medals, but I had a great time with them.

Overall, it’s an amazing experience and one I’d recommend to anyone who loves story-driven action games with heart.

Fantastic game, easily one of (if not my) favourite from the PS4 exclusives era. Playing again on PC is definitely worth it if you enjoyed it the first time round but, like me, suffer with low FPS and controller aiming.

I am a sucker for post-apocalyptic/zombie content, and this is the best representation of that in an open world setting in my opinion, but it is that - a zombie game. Like some other reviewers (including those from big names at the time of the games initial release) don't buy/play it and then moan that it's a zombie game. It's not trying to reinvent the wheel but what it does, it does exceptionally well. I rarely play story/single player games more than once, so the fact that I'm going through this again speaks loudly of my love for it.

Crying shame that a sequel seems to have been shot down but who knows, there's clearly a fanbase for the game and hopefully being released on PC will garner further support for a sequel down the road (hopefully on PC from the get-go).

TL;DR it's a fantastic take on the zombie apocalypse genre, definitely worth playing if you're into that or even just indifferent. If you hate the genre just pass and move on.

Still, it's a great game and i spent 12 hours in a session playing when i bought it, i'm just kind of an asshole and nitpick everything, just enjoy the game because it's really fun.

10 out of 10 game: incredible huge open world, great touching story, well-developed characters, great gameplay (shooting and fighting mechanics), perfect graphics.

I bought this game thinking “okay, just another zombie open-world game, nothing special.”

Now I’m emotionally attached to a broken man, addicted to a motorcycle, and personally victimized by a bunch of infected people who run faster than my life decisions.

Days Gone is basically:

“I’ll just do one mission” → 6 hours later I’m still riding my bike in the dark praying I don’t run out of fuel
“That’s a small group of enemies” → entire ecosystem collapses into screaming chaos
“Stealth approach” → accidentally sneeze → war starts

Deacon St. John talks to himself so much I started replying out loud. At some point I wasn’t sure if he needed therapy or I did.

And the hordes…
Nobody warned me that “horde” actually means “nature documentary about how quickly you can accept death.”

First encounter:
RUN.

Second encounter:
RUN FASTER.

Third encounter:
Okay maybe I can fight them.

Fourth encounter:
WHY DID I THINK THAT.

Despite all that, the game is weirdly addictive. The motorcycle travel, the survival tension, and the “one more mission” trap are dangerously well made.

It’s not a perfect game, but it is a “why am I still playing at 3 AM?” type of game.

would panic-run through the woods again.

Speaking of which, this is a very high-quality project. The game evoked interest, excitement, joy, anger, sadness and surprise.
Beautiful cinematic graphics, photo mod is cool, beautiful and atmospheric world, which is something special, a place where you want to return even after finishing the game, riding a bike is mesmerizing, clashes with zombies are very cool and, of course, the plot is very good. Days Gone is a game that has captured my heart and soul. I have played it three times, twice on the PlayStation 4 and once on PC, and I can’t get enough of it.
The game has so many things to love: the mechanics, the storytelling, the world building, and the character development. The game feels realistic and immersive, with a dynamic weather system, a day-night cycle, and a bike that needs constant maintenance and fuel. The combat is satisfying and challenging, with a variety of weapons and enemies to face. The story is emotional and engaging, with flashbacks that reveal Deacon and Sarah’s relationship and missions that advance the plot and reveal the secrets behind the outbreak. The characters are well-written and memorable, with each one having a backstory and a personality. I felt invested in their fates and their interactions with Deacon. I’m also very disappointed that we will never get a sequel. The game ends with a cliffhanger that leaves me wanting more.
